title: Grease a driveshaft slip joint: three shots through its grease fitting with a hand grease gun
instruction: Give the slip joint's grease fitting three shots from the grease gun, then put the gun back on its mat.
context: Chassis lubrication is routine vehicle service: O*NET lists "Perform routine and scheduled maintenance services, such as oil changes, lubrications, and tune-ups" as a core task of automotive service technicians and mechanics (SOC 49-3023, 676,570 employed, BLS OEWS May 2023) and heavy vehicle specialists (SOC 49-3031, 294,000 employed). Overhauling driveshaft slip joints on bench fixtures is standard overhaul practice per OEM manuals (Dana Spicer DSSM-0100, Meritor MM-96147). A greasable joint is filled through a grease fitting: the gun's coupler must sit square and fully home on the fitting while the other hand pumps the lever, because a coupler that is cocked or not home pushes grease out beside the fitting rather than into the joint, and the count matters (too little leaves splines dry, too much blows the joint seal). The robot must hold the tool seated on a 6.6 mm fitting against its weight and pumping push, pump three full strokes with the other arm, and return the gun.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), heights above the bench top. Engine off, driveshaft out of the vehicle: its slip joint is strapped to two steel bench stands and cannot turn or move. Slip joint (steel): a 5.0 cm barrel, 25 cm long, axis along x at y 12.5, 7.0 cm up, from x 25 to x 50, with a 5.8 cm dust cap at the near end and the yoke ears at the far end; two stands 4 x 9 x 4.5 cm at x 37.5 and x 46.5, a red strap over the barrel at each. Grease fitting (zinc-plated steel): one straight 1/4-28 SAE J534 fitting screwed into the barrel's side at x 30, pointing along -y, axis 7.0 cm up: 8.0 mm hex to 4.0 mm from the barrel, 4.8 mm neck to 7.0 mm, head to 11.5 mm (6.6 mm at its widest, a steep shoulder behind, a rounded nose in front). Grease gun (0.61 kg, loaded, primed, coupler not under pressure): a 3 oz pistol-grip gun (for identification only: K Tool International KTI73930 class, 13 in long), lying on its side with its axis along y at x 30: red 4.2 cm barrel 12.5 cm long, black pump head 3.6 x 4.5 x 3.4 cm, a 10 cm rigid steel pipe and a standard four-jaw coupler (1.5 cm across, 3.8 cm long, 7.2 mm bore); the coupler's mouth starts at y -4.5, 13 cm short of the fitting's nose and 4.6 cm below its axis. The fixed handle (11 cm) and the pump lever (10 cm, sprung, 18 degrees of travel, released 20 degrees off the handle) point toward the robot (-x) from the pump head. The four jaws sit just inside the mouth on radial springs (600 N/m, 0.6 N preload, 1.3 mm travel) and stand 1.0 mm into the bore; pushing the coupler on takes about 5 N, pulling it straight off about 10 N. Mat: fixed black rubber, 19 x 38 x 0.3 cm, centred at x 24.5, y -21.5; the gun starts on it.
scoring: From the recorded poses, at 20 Hz. Home: the coupler's mouth 3.6 to 5.2 mm from the barrel surface (4.5 mm when the fitting's nose is on the coupler's seat), its centre within 1.2 mm of the fitting's axis, its axis within 6 degrees of the fitting's, and all four jaws within 0.4 mm of closed (behind the head's shoulder). Coupled: home for 0.25 s. A stroke is the lever going from under 4 degrees to 15 degrees or more (of 18). A stroke is a shot into the fitting if the coupler is home from its start to that point; any other stroke is spilt (grease pushed out beside the fitting). Grease is not simulated; a real physical trial verifies delivery using macro video monitoring of coupler seating and stroke displacement, collects expelled grease on pre-weighed absorbent wipes, and measures grease mass delivery on a 0.01 g analytical balance against the calibrated ~0.85 g/stroke metered gun output. Score at the end: 0 if never coupled; else 0.10 + 0.20 per shot into the fitting up to three, -0.20 per shot beyond three, -0.10 if any stroke was spilt; +0.15 if the coupler is off the fitting (mouth 2 cm or more from the fitting's nose, jaws closed); and then +0.15 if the gun lies on the mat (axis within 12 degrees of level, wholly over the mat, within 6 mm of its top), let go (every robot collision piece 2 cm or more from the gun's bounding box) and still. 1.0 held for 1 s is success. 0, and it stays 0: six shots into the fitting (the joint's seal is blown), or the gun dropped off the bench (5 cm or more below the top). Range 0 to 1.
reset_notes: Lay the gun on its side on the mat, on its axis line, mouth at y -4.5 cm, handle and lever toward the robot; the lever springs back by itself and the jaws close by themselves. Real trial: wipe the fitting and the coupler, bleed the joint or swap the stub so the three shots start from the same fill, and weigh the gun.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The four jaws are free 20 g bodies on sprung radial slides and hold by contact on a convex fitting head (friction 0.12); nothing latches by proximity. Real jaws lock harder once the coupler is under pressure. Grease, pressure and the fitting's ball check are not simulated: a shot is a full lever stroke with the coupler home, and the lever resists with its return spring only (about 13 N at the grip). Barrel, pipe and fitting are octagonal.
